text: 15. This microscopic mite is a close relative of the common eyelash mite but chooses a slightly different niche. It bypasses the hair follicles to live deeper within the skin, specifically inside the sebaceous glands that produce natural oils. They remain hidden during the day and only emerge onto the surface at night to find a mate before returning to their oily environment. What is this specific species?

16. This biological fact is often used to highlight the "gross factor" of the Demodex mites that inhabit the skin. Because these mites lack a specific anatomical feature for waste disposal, they are incapable of eliminating metabolic byproducts throughout their lives. Instead, all waste accumulates within their bodies and is only released into the pore when the mite dies and decomposes. What anatomical feature do they lack?
